sections.name: SCOTTSDALE, AZ 85251
sentences: This matter is brought pursuant to Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended (Title VII), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA) and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act. Jurisdiction is based on 28 U.S.C. $ 1331 and 1343, Jurisdiction is also based diversity of citizenship pursuant to 28 U.S. c.s 1332 and the amount in question exceeds $75,000.00 (seventy five thousand dollars and zero cents) exclusive of interests and costs.
Jurisdiction for the state law claim is invoked pursuant to 28 U.S.C. S 1367(a) to hear and adjudicate state law claims.

sections.name: FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
sentences: Plaintiff was born on July 29, 1959/and is currently 62 years old; She is African American and female.

Plaintiff became employed by defendant in on/around October 30, 2016 as a licensed care coordinator. | Atall times relevant to this complaint and at all times relevant to her employment with defendant, which ended on November 4, 2019, plaintiff was well qualified for her sokition and performed them ina satisfactory manner.

In/around 2019 plaintiff, whose duties included interviewing clients with mental health issues and documenting those interviews, proposed a procedure to her supervisor, Debra Sheppard, a Caucasian female, who approved the procedure.
The procedure allowed to “cutting and pasting” part of a template used to document sessions/interviews with clients that would remain consistent.
Somehow, plaintiff accidentally failed to document a template after an | interview, which the defendant stated it observed during an office audit.

Defendant suspended and then fired plaintiff on November 4, 2019; however it took no disciplinary action against Ms. Sheppard (who is | (was) also under the age of 40). | Prior to plaintiff's termination from pmployment, her team lead, a Caucasian female, Ms. Jody Sanford had frequently stated that there were multiple individuals in paint department who were no pulling their weight — however no correctivd action was taken regarding those individuals; conversely before her error, plaintiff had worked excellently at all times.

Defendants’ managerial employees admitted during the audit that other personnel had made errors documenting interviews with clients, however those individuals were not fired, as plaintiff was. Defendant characterized plaintiffs’ error as falsification of documents, indicating that it determined that plaintiff had committed the error intentionally; defendant unsuccessfully fought plaintiffs application for unemployment compensation on that basis.
Ms. Sanford allegedly conducted the audit that resulted in plaintiff's termination from employment.

Inan attempt to remain employed, plaintiff requested from several of defendants management personne that they place herona | ‘performance improvement plan (PIP), including to Ms. Sheppard, Ms. Sanford, Ms. Kaila Mailhan, a Caucasian female manager, and Ms. Janet Edwards, a Caucasian (the Director), lidicating that she had merely made a mistake that she had not corgmitted fraud.
Despite plaintiff's plea, Ms. Mailhan insisted that she be fired and that she had committed fraud — intentional acts.

Ms. Sheppard admitted at plaintiff's unemployment compensation hearing that other of defendant’s employees had been found to have made errors, during the audit and Ms. Sheppard admitted that plaintiff's error was unintentional.
One of the employees who committed error, was Steven Bussey, a male employee, whom had a meeting with management, but was not fired.

Upon reasonable information and belief, other employees who were found to have made documentation errors during the audit, were Caucasian, male, and under the age of forty, or significantly younger than the plaintiff. | | Plaintiff perceived that her “ve process and interaction with defendant’s management indicated some form of discriminatory bias, since it was extremely hostile, although plaintiff had an excellent record | and a good attitude (this includes bias based on her race and/or her age).

Plaintiff is aware that persons in hef protected classes have been fired or left their employment with the defendant under specious circumstances, including an African American (Black) manager named Kimberly Webb, who was replaced with Debra Sheppard, who had previously worked with Director Janet Edwards (a Caucasian female).

After her termination, olaintiff saw her job posted for $20,000.00 less than what he had earned per year, and believes that this was to hire someone under the age of forty, or considerably younger than she, who might work for much less than she was earning — upon information and belief, plaintiff was replaced by someone under the age of forty or considerably younger than she. Defendant has a history of laying off employees over the age of forty, including in 2017, when the entire management team that started the | Filed 11/15/21 Page 9 of 13 | Intensive Case Management Program was terminated when the company was consolidating including, Eileen O’Reagan, Kay Cox and another woman believed to be over forty.
Each of the women referred to in peragraph 24 above had over 20 years of employment with the defendant.
Other older employees have resigned due to harassment and being give unrealistic work expectations.
These included an Indian American manager, named Nishma Daya.
Another Black manager named Rosalind Brunson resigned due to harassment from management; another older female employee resigned due to alleged harassment.

Upon information and belief, defendant has/had a progressive disciplinary policy which it could have utilized for the plaintiff, and which it uses for individuals who aré not members in her protected classes, but which it refused to use for her based on discrimination based on either her age, sex or race (or a combination of some of all of them).

Upon information and belief, employees who have committed a intentional misconduct or errors worpe than plaintiff, have not been fired by the defendant, despite its knwledge of that conduct and those errors.
As a result of defendant’s conduct described above, plaintiff suffered severe economic harm, including thelloss of her career.
Asa result of defendant’s plaintiff suffered severe emotional distress, including based on loss of her personal reputation for honesty, and other severe emotional distress.

sections.name: COUNT ONE — VIOLATION OF TITLE Vil BASED ON SEX AND/OR RACE
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-32 above as though fully set forth herein.
Plaintiff is African American and female, and she was qualified for her position, when she was unjustly fired.

Defendant fired plaintiff for alleged conduct which it knew she did not commit; it fired her for something that it has not fired employees who have committed the same, similar or worse things than plaintiff, who are male and who are not African American, which it did intentionally.

Defendant intentionally discriminated against plaintiff based on her | race and sex. | WHEREFORE, plaintiff requests judgment in her favor against defendant, and she requests the following relief: | a. Back pay; b. Front pay; c. Compensatory damages; d. Punitive damages; e. Reasonable Attorney’s Fees and Costs; f. Any other relief the Court deems appropriate.
